newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet sees $0.07 unit cost over time.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet sees $0.07 unit cost over time.

text.p: ValuJet Inc President Lewis Jordan said on Monday that the discount carrier should be able to achieve a unit cost of only $0.07 per available seat mile (ASM) over time.

"Seven cents is the number I said we should be able to get to by the time we are at steady-state, up in maybe the 30-airplane level or above. We know it will be higher than that for a while," he told reporters while preparing to board the carrier's first scheduled flight in more than three months.

Analysts say ValuJet had an ASM unit cost of just $0.0695 during the first quarter of the year, months before the May 11 Everglades crash of Flight 592 that prompted the federal investigations and inspections that finally forced its grounding in mid-June.
Reports of widespread maintenance problems at the airline led analysts to assume ValuJet would no longer be able to operate at such low costs.
Jordan declined to discuss expected unit costs at the relaunch of the airline. An analyst last week said ValuJet's costs could be near eight cents per ASM.
